title: S&P Select Sector Indices December rebalance — reference close (prices the capping trade that prints into the 2027-12-17 witching close)
source: EST: date derived by applying an SEC-filed rule to the 2027 calendar, with the rule RE-FETCHED AND RE-READ THIS SESSION rather than inherited from the calendar's March sibling. SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497 (accession 0001193125-26-031948, d85739d497.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes), verbatim: 'The rebalancing of the Select Sector Indices, based on the processes described above, occurs at the closing prices of the second Friday of March, June, September and December. Changes will become effective after the market close on the third Friday of March, June, September and December.' The second Friday of December 2027 is 2027-12-10 and the third Friday is 2027-12-17 (weekday arithmetic recomputed mechanically this session — December 2027's Fridays are the 3rd, 10th, 17th, 24th and 31st; the third Friday is independently confirmed on OCC's own 2027 calendar by opex-2027-12-17). Filed estimate rather than SEC:/confirmed on the same two counts the calendar's own sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12 records: the filing dates the RULE, not this instance — no 2027-dated S&P DJI or SPDR announcement was fetched — and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-quarterly-rebalance-effective-2027-12-20 initial research (2026-09-08). This is the December sibling of an event the calendar already tracks for March 2027 (sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12) and for December 2026 (a proposal, from-sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31), and it is missing for the quarter the proposer researches. WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER: the same 497 sentence dates the Select Sector rebalance effective 'after the market close on the third Friday of ... December', i.e. at the 2027-12-17 close — the same close at which the S&P DJI quarterly rebalance the proposer researches is implemented, and the same close as the opex-2027-12-17 quarterly expiration. This Friday's prints are what those managers must trade one week later, so it is the pricing date for the one concentrated single-name component of that auction. SIZE, CARRIED FORWARD FROM THE MARCH LEDGER AND NOT RE-MEASURED HERE: on State Street's own holdings files for all eleven Select Sector SPDRs, the CAPPING component runs ~$1.10B one-way against $391B of assets — a concentrated ~$1B trade sitting inside a much larger and duller share/float housekeeping trade, not the largest mechanical component of the witching auction outright. WHAT THE PROPOSER MEASURED ABOUT THE CORRIDOR, so a taking lane does not inherit an expectation: SPY's December third-Friday relative volume is the largest of the four quarterly legs (1.639x mean / 1.789x median vs 1.420x / 1.377x for Mar/Jun/Sep, 16 of 21 above 1.0x), but that December premium over the other QUARTERLY legs is NOT established (Mann-Whitney p=13.6%, n=21); only the step over an ordinary monthly opex Friday is (p=1.89%). Treat the December witching close as a quarterly-sized execution hazard, not a December-sized one, until a lane measures it with more than 21 draws. Low impact and market-structure only: it changes execution timing, never direction, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is rebalance-, opex- or index-flow-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-08, zero hits). Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
